Chapter 9: Advanced Practices—Expanding Awareness and Cultivating Equanimity
As your mindfulness practice matures, you’ll start to notice that brand new possibilities begin to open up.
Instead of keeping your attention just on the breath or the body, you can expand your focus to include a much wider range of experiences—like sounds, thoughts, emotions, and even the simple flow of awareness itself.
Why do this? Because broadening your practice like this helps you develop something truly valuable: equanimity. That’s a balanced, steady mind that doesn’t get thrown off so easily when things change.
One way to deepen your practice is through open awareness—sometimes folks call it “choiceless awareness.” Imagine this: instead of locking your attention onto just one thing, you let your awareness rest on whatever pops up. It could be a sound in the distance, a physical sensation, a thought, or a fleeting feeling.
Your mind becomes like a wide, open field—receptive to everything, not clinging to anything, and not pushing anything away.
Another powerful practice is working with strong emotions. Rather than running from tough feelings or trying to suppress them, you actually invite them into your awareness.
You notice where these emotions show up in your body, you watch how they shift and change, and—most importantly—you allow them to be there without judging yourself.
With time, even the most intense emotions start to lose their grip, and you realize you’re not as easily overwhelmed as before.
So, what exactly is equanimity? Well, it’s not about being numb or indifferent.
It’s more like having deep roots—like a sturdy tree that stays grounded, even when the winds of life blow. You’re steady, open, and able to meet both the highs and the lows with a kind of gentle strength.
Let’s talk about a few ways you can start building these advanced mindfulness skills in your own life:
First, try practicing open awareness. That means setting aside a little time just to notice whatever comes up, without picking and choosing. Let every experience have its moment.
Next, when strong emotions arise, shift your attention away from the story behind them and tune in to how they feel in your body. Notice the physical sensations—maybe a tightness in your chest or fluttering in your stomach—and just let them be there.
And finally, see if you can notice the space around your experiences. Instead of getting lost in every thought or feeling, pay attention to the awareness in which all of these things are happening.
It’s a subtle shift, but it can make a world of difference.
Remember, these advanced practices aren’t separate from the basics—they’re really just deeper expressions of the same core principles. As your awareness becomes more open and stable, you might notice a real sense of freedom and ease growing within you.
The mind learns to rest in its own natural clarity, no matter what’s going on around you.
